name: comp-34
title: Character Limit Input
description: A labelled single-line text field that shows a live character count such as 0/50 inside the right edge and stops accepting input once the limit is reached.
use: Fields with a hard cap, such as a short bio or status line, where the limit must stay visible.
avoid: A single line only; longer text needs a textarea, and the counter shares the same narrow strip.
a11y: The label and live counter are tied to the field with aria-describedby, so the limit is announced as it changes. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A label above a rounded dark field on a black stage, with a faint grey counter reading 0/50 pinned inside the right edge. Typed text fills the line from the left and slides under the counter as it grows.
behaves: Typing fills the line and the counter ticks upward one digit at a time toward 50, after which no more characters are accepted. The clip grows the entry from 0/50 to 46/50 while the line scrolls to keep the caret in view.
customise: The label and the 50-character cap are fixed in the file, and the field and counter styling are classes there as well.
weight: light: One field, one counter and a change handler; nothing animates at rest.
demo: Label Input with character limit, with a draft ending look great — ship it Friday.
issues: The empty field has no placeholder, so nothing hints what the 50 characters are for.
polishWhy: Tidy field with a clear live counter, but the demo is a bare text line.
